holisticNarrative.summary:
The evidence set for SequelMed EHR export is compact: one short PDF plus a landing-page screenshot. The PDF is clear about two operational facts: both single-patient and multi-patient exports are available without developer assistance, and each patient export package includes a clinical C-CDA XML file plus a documents folder and a Patient Documents Detail.xls file. Those are direct signals that a customer-run extraction path exists.

Implementation detail remains thin. There is no published data dictionary, no explicit field inventory, no key/relationship map, no value-set bindings, and no sample payload. The spreadsheet component is named but never explained, creating uncertainty about whether it is only a document manifest or a richer metadata structure. The structured clinical payload is explicitly C-CDA, which helps interoperability but strongly signals projection behavior rather than broad operational-model exposure.

Applying designated-record-set EHI scope, the core concern is potential underrepresentation of patient-decision and billing-relevant data. Claims/billing, payments, and explicit order/referral lifecycle structures are weakly evidenced or absent in the public export documentation. In contrast, operational categories such as scheduling and audit logs were intentionally not treated as EHI gaps in this abstraction.
standoutObservations: Surprising: a multi-patient export path is explicitly claimed in the same short artifact that otherwise provides minimal technical detail.
Risky: Patient Documents Detail.xls is listed but not documented, leaving a key potential linkage artifact opaque.
Important boundary: audit/provenance omission was not treated as an EHI completeness failure under designated-record-set scoping.

notableFacts: SequelMed export documentation explicitly states both single-patient and multi-patient EHI export can be executed at any time without developer assistance.
Each patient export is documented as a compressed zip containing exactly three top-level components: Clinical folder, Documents folder, and Patient Documents Detail.xls.
Structured clinical content is explicitly described as one XML-based C-CDA file per patient with references to C-CDA R2.1 implementation guides.
Documents folder explicitly lists signed progress notes, available lab results, radiology reports, and scanned/imported/uploaded documents with original file formats retained.
No public field-level schema, data dictionary, relationship map, or sample payload artifact was found in the collected evidence set.
